after.text: Ḥamara ṣərāʾ retains the selected expression ሐመረ፡ ጽራእ untranslated in transliteration because its complete meaning is unresolved. Actual primary Dillmann1865 column76 discusses this compound and explicitly cites32:4; column1275 calls its second element uncertain and questions whether it is a tree name or a form related to a name for Greece. Those discussions do not establish pine, carob, tamarind, cherry, a modern species or one secure English gloss. This is an explicitly provisional critical treatment, not a claim that the lexical problem is solved. No different-edition reading or Greek height/leaf clause is silently supplied.

The selected fruit comparison uses the vine-cluster expression. The correct primary cross-reference is column752 to378, where the noun has collective and singular uses with plural forms separately listed. “A cluster of grapes” is a bounded rendering of that range, not a claim that the passage counts exactly one cluster. An earlier95 locator was a neighbouring-entry error and is not positive lexical proof. The selected good/beautiful expression is rendered once; no Greek leaf-comparison clause is added.
